analysis.title: JPM Tyler - Morning Briefing: Tactically Bullish with updated Monetization Menu; Positioning; 26Q3 Earnings Preview 28 Sep 2026
key_insights: JPM Market Intel returns to a Tactically Bullish view after moving Cautious/Neutral on Aug 31. Since that call SPX is +75bp and the long NDX / short RTY pair returned 7.9%. The setup is judged more favorable as bond yields find a level and oil trends lower in a choppy fashion.

Rationale for the bullish view: Flash PMIs show stronger growth than priced in, consumer spending is defying expectations, 26Q3 earnings expectations (~29% growth) may prove light, yields may stabilize, and technicals are improving (seasonality, possible retail participation, light positioning).

Monetization Menu update: still like Tech as a core long (Semis and Mag7 potentially outperforming the Tech tape, Software a non-consensus bullish play), but no longer pair it with an RTY short because of squeeze risk from lower oil and yields. A derivative expression is suggested to play the squeeze.

Ex-Tech, a persistent cyclical rally needs yield curve bull steepening. Excluding AI plays, JPM favors Banks (growth reboot, potentially steeper curve, capital markets outlook). Real Estate, Telecom and Utilities may join a squeeze but are expected to lag the SPX ex-AI. The COVID Reopening theme (Airlines, Autos, Cruise Lines, Discretionary, Hotels) is of interest, preferably via options.

Last week SPX gained 1.2% to ~55bp from ATH, NDX gained 3.3% and set a new ATH Tuesday, RTY lost 80bp. WTI fell 3.8% to $92.41 but the 10Y yield rose, +41bp MTD, as bond vol spiked. Flash PMIs point to economy growing at ~5% pace.

Three US/Iran scenarios: (1) deal this week gives a short squeeze rally led by RTY with energy prices collapsing and the curve bull steepening, EU outperforms US. (2) No deal, no escalation keeps AI/Tech leading, NDX > EU > SPX, yields range-bound. (3) No deal with escalation means $100 oil and 10Y above 5%, equities lower.

Trump rejected the Iranian proposal to return to the MoU and says kinetic action is likely to resume post-Midterms, but talks continue and are moving to a more technical phase. Iran's president said Iran wants a deal before the US midterm election.

Monday pre-market: futures lower with Tech underperforming on higher oil and another surge in bond yields. 10Y at 5.226%, WTI at $95.51, VIX 16.32. Memory/Semis lead the Tech selling. Defensives lead Cyclicals.

Short-term catalysts: PCE and ISM-Mfg this week (ISM Prices Paid is a forward inflation indicator, hotter prints could bear flatten the curve), NFP on Oct 2, AI datapoints (Meta Muse release, OpenAI Dev Day, MU earnings), and Tokyo CPI and China PMIs. CPI is Oct 14 and the Fed Oct 28.

Longer-term concerns: the bond market may underprice Fed hikes given ~5% real growth and inflation pressure, the market may begin pricing a 50bp hike at some meeting, ag inflation may bleed into core, and it is unclear whether anything besides Tech works. The market is in a 'Good News is Bad News' mode on labor data.

FactSet earnings preview: 26Q3 expected at 11.9% revenue growth, 28.9% earnings growth, 15.0% margins. 26Q4 expected 11.7% revenue and 2.5% earnings growth. FY26 12.1% revenue and 31.8% EPS growth. FY27 9.1% revenue and 15.2% EPS growth. 26Q2 saw 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% earnings growth and 17% margins.

Macro: Flash Composite PMI printed a 5-year high, pointing to ~5% real GDP growth, the strongest since 2015 excluding COVID. Supply chain bottlenecks are among the worst in the survey's history excluding COVID, with hiring increasing, pointing to stronger inflation. SPX earnings growth moves with nominal GDP.
Feroli forecasts NFP +100k with unemployment steady at 4.1% (risk of lower), JOLTS 7.40mm vs 7.27mm, core PCE +0.25% m/m (3.3% y/y) and ISM-Mfg 54.5 vs 54.6 prior.

Oil: Henrici says throughput is ~10mm bpd up from a 2mm bpd trough, so a deal is unlikely to trigger as large a crude decline as the 20%+ drop from mid-May to late-June, implying a choppy, weaker trend. There is moderate diesel demand destruction in airlines and trucking.

A US diesel export ban could cut diesel from ~$6.50/gal to $4.70 after 15 days and $4.00 after 60 days, but a ban longer than 30 days would compress refining margins. Gulf Coast supply lacks pipelines to the East Coast where demand is highest.

Positioning: gross flows fell (-0.6z globally, APAC -1.7z), net flows mixed with strong Asia selling. US TPM at -0.1z / 40th percentile, EU TPM at 17th percentile. Utilities HF net exposure at a historical low (-2.5z), Telecom at historical lows, Real Estate near 12m low.
Health Care crowding performance fell further (L-S spread -7% past 5d). Clinical Biotech sold ~2z over 1wk, positioning at ~12m lows, while Commercial Biotech saw ~2z net buying on short covering.

Financials saw HF buy-the-dip buying (+2z), led by Insurance. Large Cap Banks were bought while Regionals continued to be sold. Mag7 bought ~3z over 5d, Semis +2z, Software +1z, with retail Semis vs Software sentiment rebounding to about average.

JPM FICC (Barry): neutral on duration, with a less strong bearish bias. Maintain 10s/20s/30s belly-cheapening butterflies and 2Yx3Y zero-coupon inflation swap shorts, initiate 10-year IOTA longs. Rates implied vol is near YTD highs but patience is advised before selling vol. For shorts, sell 6Mx30Y straddles vs buying vega-neutral 1Yx30Y straddles, delta hedged daily.
Treasury supply: $380bn net bill issuance expected mid-October through Thanksgiving, with TGA briefly above $1.05tn in late October, bringing reserves below $2.9tn.

Credit: HG spreads are resilient and look ~7bp too tight, and rate vol suggests 5-10bp wider. HY yields are above 8% for the first time since Liberation Day, spreads 9bp wider on the week. Leveraged loans are outperforming bonds by +203bp in September, the widest margin in four years.
FICC: Barry sees yields rising ahead of the first hike and peaking 2-3 months later, with curve flattening stronger than typical. Meera is bullish USD on cheap valuations.
EU/UK: UK Homebuilders basket +11.7% (+5.8z) after a new government loan program for first-time buyers. Value/Quality lead, Growth/Momentum lag.
